title: Build a Retail Systematic Desk, Safely

episodes.title: Freeze the Scope Before You Write Code
episodes.subtitle: A narrow mandate prevents a prototype from quietly becoming an uncontrolled trading desk.

episodes.title: Define Non-Goals and Kill Criteria
episodes.subtitle: A safe system states what it refuses to optimize and when it must stop.

episodes.title: Choose a Boring First Market
episodes.subtitle: The best learning environment is liquid, observable and operationally simple.

episodes.title: Draw Hard System Boundaries
episodes.subtitle: Data collection, strategy decisions and broker actions should be separate services.

episodes.title: Facts, Decisions and Orders Are Different Objects
episodes.subtitle: Keeping three records prevents explanations from mutating into instructions.

episodes.title: Let Each Layer Fail Without Lying
episodes.subtitle: Partial failure should remain visible instead of becoming a clean but false result.

episodes.title: Discover Capabilities at Runtime
episodes.subtitle: A client should ask what a service can do instead of trusting last month's schema.

episodes.title: Make Freshness a Blocking Field
episodes.subtitle: Collected now does not mean the underlying market observation is current.

episodes.title: Preserve Partial Failures in Batches
episodes.subtitle: One bad symbol must not erase nine valid cells or make the batch look complete.

episodes.title: Resolve Identity Before You Use a Ticker
episodes.subtitle: The same symbol can refer to different instruments across venues and time.

episodes.title: Treat Time as a First-Class Field
episodes.subtitle: Event time, observation time and ingestion time answer different questions.

episodes.title: Corporate Events Can Change the Instrument
episodes.subtitle: Splits, mergers and distributions are data transformations, not footnotes.

episodes.title: Use One Snapshot for One Decision
episodes.subtitle: Mixing data cuts makes a precise-looking plan impossible to reproduce.

episodes.title: Hash the Evidence, Not the Narrative
episodes.subtitle: Integrity comes from binding decisions to files and fields, not from confident prose.

episodes.title: Replay Without Re-Querying
episodes.subtitle: A reproducible run consumes a frozen bundle instead of asking the market again.

episodes.title: Screen Broad, Then Narrow With Evidence
episodes.subtitle: Cheap deterministic filters should precede expensive research.

episodes.title: Zero Candidates Is a Valid Outcome
episodes.subtitle: Forcing a quota converts selectivity into hidden risk.

episodes.title: Explain Every Rejection
episodes.subtitle: A rejected candidate is useful feedback when the failed gate is explicit.

episodes.title: Certify a Candidate With Independent Evidence
episodes.subtitle: A chart pattern is one input, not a complete trade case.

episodes.title: Test the Sector, Leaders and Blast Radius
episodes.subtitle: Peers can confirm context without becoming proof of causality.

episodes.title: Turn Price Levels Into Conditional Plans
episodes.subtitle: An entry is a market condition with an expiry, not a number to chase.

episodes.title: Put Strategy Rules in Versioned Configuration
episodes.subtitle: Code should execute a declared contract, not hide tunable behavior.

episodes.title: Persist State, Validity and Revisions
episodes.subtitle: A stateful strategy cannot be reconstructed safely from broker positions alone.

episodes.title: Use a Complete Machine-Readable Plan
episodes.subtitle: Execution should receive quantities, protections and gates, not an investment story.

episodes.title: Backtest on Frozen Point-in-Time Data
episodes.subtitle: A fast simulation is useless if it sees information the trader could not know.

episodes.title: Model Costs, Gaps and Partial Fills
episodes.subtitle: Close-to-close arithmetic is not an execution model.

episodes.title: Use Baselines, Walk-Forward and Stress Tests
episodes.subtitle: A backtest matters only relative to simple alternatives and unseen periods.

episodes.title: Size at the Portfolio Level
episodes.subtitle: Per-trade loss is only one ceiling on position size.

episodes.title: Find Correlation and Hidden Factor Bets
episodes.subtitle: Ten tickers can still be one concentrated position.

episodes.title: Gate Event Risk and Add Kill Switches
episodes.subtitle: Known events and system health should override the urge to deploy capital.

episodes.title: Simulate the Broker Before Connecting One
episodes.subtitle: The simulator is a contract test for the desk, not a return generator.

episodes.title: Build an Explicit Order State Machine
episodes.subtitle: Orders move through states; they do not jump from submitted to done.

episodes.title: Test Restarts, Duplicates and Broken Networks
episodes.subtitle: A robust client assumes it will lose the response at the worst moment.

episodes.title: Use an Append-Only Decision Ledger
episodes.subtitle: Corrections should add records, not rewrite the history they explain.

episodes.title: Design Recovery and Supersession
episodes.subtitle: A restart must know which plan, revision and protection are active.

episodes.title: Make Every Run Auditable
episodes.subtitle: A quiet day and a crashed pipeline need different evidence.

episodes.title: Check Broker Capabilities Before Placement
episodes.subtitle: Account and venue support must be discovered for every execution run.

episodes.title: Make Placement Idempotent
episodes.subtitle: Every retry must reconcile first and remain blocked when broker acceptance is unknown.

episodes.title: Reconcile Intent With Broker Reality
episodes.subtitle: The broker record wins on fills, while the plan remains the source of intended behavior.

episodes.title: Put the Decision and Controls First
episodes.subtitle: The first viewport should answer what, why, when and what blocks action.

episodes.title: Make Missing Data Actionable
episodes.subtitle: Unavailable is useful only when the interface explains impact and recovery.

episodes.title: Use Alerts That Lead to Decisions
episodes.subtitle: An alert should identify impact, required action and urgency.

episodes.title: Keep the Language Model Out of Arithmetic
episodes.subtitle: Use AI for interpretation and review, while code owns numbers and state.

episodes.title: Use Adversarial Review as a Release Gate
episodes.subtitle: Different reviewers should attack correctness, risk and usability on the same snapshot.

episodes.title: Promote From Replay to Live in Stages
episodes.subtitle: The capstone is a controlled operating process, not an autonomous bot.
